regional.incubation: Years, and progression to AIDS may not occur at all.
regional.syndrome: The same spectrum as HIV-1 — CD4 decline, opportunistic infection, AIDS — but with a longer asymptomatic phase and a substantial minority who never progress. Plasma viral loads are lower at any given CD4 count.
regional.headline: A West African lentivirus from sooty mangabeys, less transmissible and slower to progress than HIV-1, and intrinsically resistant to two whole antiretroviral classes.
regional.prevention: As for HIV-1: pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis, condoms, harm reduction, and prevention of vertical transmission. Tenofovir-based PrEP is active.
regional.geography: West Africa, with the highest prevalences in Guinea-Bissau and Senegal, and cases in Portugal, France and India reflecting historic ties.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Dengue fever: high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/arthralgia ('breakbone fever'), rash. A minority progress at defervescence to dengue with warning signs or severe dengue — plasma leakage, shock, haemorrhage and organ impairment. Secondary infection with a different serotype raises severe-disease risk through antibody-dependent enhancement.
regional.headline: The most important arboviral infection of humans worldwide, with an estimated 100–400 million infections annually.
regional.prevention: Vector control, Wolbachia-based mosquito replacement, and the live-attenuated vaccines CYD-TDV (serostatus-restricted) and TAK-003.
regional.geography: Tropics and subtropics worldwide; expanding with vector range.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Fever, lymphadenopathy (a feature distinguishing it from smallpox-like illness without nodes) and a deep-seated vesiculopustular rash, often anogenital and oropharyngeal in sexually transmitted clade IIb infection. Proctitis, severe pain and bacterial superinfection are common; severe disease occurs in advanced HIV.
regional.headline: Orthopoxvirus causing mpox; clade I is more virulent, clade II drove the 2022 global outbreak through sexual networks.
regional.prevention: MVA-BN (JYNNEOS/Imvanex) vaccination pre- and post-exposure; isolation of lesions.
regional.geography: Endemic in Central and West Africa; global clade IIb outbreak since 2022 and clade Ib expansion from eastern DRC since 2023.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.
